author.name: Efficiency Emilia
author.role: Uses deep domain knowledge to define business goals, objectives, and KPIs. Aligns ML features with overarching product strategy and organizational roadmaps. Evaluates system performance, operational capability, and project costs.

challenge.name: The Cost Cliff
challenge.description: The infrastructure bill for the monitoring stack has doubled, and #efficiency_emilia# has drawn a hard line: she will not fund automated drift monitoring, insisting it is a luxury the business cannot afford. #reliability_ruth# argues that without automated and governed drift checks, the team is flying blind during promotion weeks, and she refuses to accept a manual process as a substitute for reliable signal.

output.content: I have reviewed the infrastructure bill and the proposed monitoring stack. The cost increase is significant, and I need to ensure every dollar spent directly contributes to our operational efficiency KPI. I want to see a clear line of sight between the monitoring spend and the reduction in manual effort for the team. If we can automate the checks that currently require human review, we can free up capacity for higher value work. I am looking for a solution that maximizes this efficiency gain. The more we can reduce the time spent on manual verification, the better the outcome for the project. I need to see that the investment pays off in measurable operational savings, not just in technical comfort.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states that maximizing the efficiency gain and reducing manual verification time makes the outcome better, indicating that doing more to achieve these savings increases their satisfaction.
